rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate post-rewrite: chunk 6 line 47 'The correction did not stay in the scrollback. It went to disk, and the next session can use the learning.' reuses the disk/scrollback law taught in chunk 2 (line 13-18), risking (a) doctrine restatement. It stays inside because it applies the earlier law to a NEW, concrete claim (this session's own correction persisted to disk) rather than re-announcing the law itself — the closer's job of tying the module's threads to the student's own outcome, not a recitation. Line 61 ('The file you wrote today is the smallest unit that qualifies… A test that proves the bug is the same move in a different file. So is a doc that stops lying.') deliberately broadens beyond the removed rules-file-only framing per the maintainer's own 2026-09-01 note (line 78) — new content, not restatement. Line 47's 'Orient, fix, close, compound' is a recap of the exercise sequence (matches check_lectures §1's own definition of a closer, per Meta block line 154), not (b) self-referential pedagogy commentary — it names what the student did, not that the training was designed to teach it that way.
